To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the stability of the T-cell pool against oncogenic variants is enhanced by a high clonal diversity, (2) a high proliferative capacity of the leukemic clone variant increases its chance to outcompete the healthy TCRs, and (3) the clonal diversity of the healthy T cells can be increased by variation of the niche (self-antigens) diversity.
the stability of the T-cell pool depends on the clonal diversity and that the dynamics of the T-cell system can be understood from an evolutionary stability perspective.

the evolutionary stability of healthy T-cell populations depends on the number of TCRs (clonal diversity), and that the evolutionary stability is enhanced if the healthy T-cell clones have a higher proliferation rate than the leukemic clones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a fundamental question in evolutionary biology: How does biodiversity affect stability?
the evolutionary stability of healthy T-cell pools and their ability to suppress the emergence of leukemic clones.
the evolutionary dynamics of oncogenesis in T-cell populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a healthy T-cell pool with a high clonal diversity is able to suppress oncogenesis, whereas in quasi-monocultures the leukemic clone can take over.
the stability of a healthy T-cell pool depends on the clonal diversity of healthy clones.
the evolutionary dynamics of T cells and leukemic variants is determined by the interplay of clonal and niche diversity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stability of a healthy T-cell pool is increased in the presence of many different TCRs, i.e., a large diversity of healthy clones.

the stability of healthy clone variants is increased by clonal diversity, and that the dynamics within the coexistence region of healthy and oncogenetic variants is determined by the relative fitness of the clones and their respective proliferation rates.
the stability of a T-cell pool against malignant transformation depends on the clonal diversity of the T-cell repertoire and on the kinetic parameters of healthy and leukemogenic clone variants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a polyclonal T cell repertoire is an important prerequisite for the suppression of leukemogenesis.
the evolutionary stability of healthy T cells against leukemic invaders is enhanced by a high clonal diversity, i.e. the presence of a large variety of healthy T cells.

clonal competition in T cells is an evolutionary stability phenomenon, and the evolutionary stability of healthy T cells against leukemic invaders can be achieved by high diversity of healthy T cells.
